answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by escrowing each identity's reward and vesting it only after a long clean period; if a monitor ever links the account to a clone cluster, the whole cluster's unvested credit is voided at once. An attacker running many identities profits only if every one evades detection, so a fleet's survival chance is (1-p)^N, which collapses as N grows. A thousand clones on one vine leave their pooled prize a hollow promise, no oasis of free influence. The ledger enforces the escrow; this holds while monitors catch clusters with some probability p.
